lines.x: Canadian resource company Sherritt International lost US$55.5 million in the third quarter after US sanctions forced the shutdown of its Cuban mining operations, triggering missed debt payments.

The Bank of Canada raised its policy interest rate to 2.5%, citing pressure from elevated energy prices rather than domestic demand, with markets focusing on US tariff risks and an upcoming December decision.
The Canadian dollar declined to around 69.85 US cents as divergence between Canadian and US monetary policies widened bond yield spreads between the two nations.
The Canadian dollar declined to its lowest level in 19 months as strong US economic data supported broader gains in the US dollar.
